$doc: Every scattered decor kind's seed and placement rules. A rule is per
ground channel: the channel's types it stands on by cube_types name, the
channels that must hold nothing (`void`), and any other channel is
anything. The scatter stays generic, so a later kind (a fence along
a road edge, a candle inside a structure, ...) is one more entry here.
Trees on green/forest terrain, and only where nothing else (water, a
structure, a road) already claims the cell — the same "what actually
renders there" precedence the terrain paint applies, since a cell whose
land channel says green_light but whose transport channel is a road is a
road, not grass.
bare is included alongside the two explicit GREEN_* types even though its
own name says "bare ground": it's the fallback land type for any cell
with no real landuse tag, and this pack's actual land_bare.png texture is
a grassy yellow-green speckle nearly indistinguishable from
land_green_light.png — visually it *is* the plain grass most of an
untagged map reads as, not dirt. SPORTS was considered too (its own
texture leans mint-green) but left out: it's a maintained field, not
natural ground, and reads wrong with trees scattered across it.
Arbitrary, fixed — only has to stay stable across sessions; a big odd
constant rather than a small number so it mixes well even before
combining with a per-page seed.
Moderate, deliberately sparse — a scattered handful of trees reading as
"this hillside has some trees on it", not a solid forest wall at 1u
spacing (which a much higher density would read as, given every eligible
cell is only 1u wide).
The kind's variants, each a model by its path under asset/, in the
order the scatter picks among them: the fantasy town kit's five trees
and the graveyard kit's four pines.
Each variant's colormap, row for row with `models`: the Kenney packs keep
the texture outside the glb and share it across the pack, and a kind's
variants can come from more than one pack.
Small boats on open water. Open river/lake water only — WETLAND is
excluded (too shallow/marshy for a boat to sit in), and
structure/transport must both still be VOID: per the terrain paint's
precedence, either one (a pier, a bridge deck) would win over water and
actually render as itself, not water, at that cell — a boat there would
visually float on top of a bridge instead of the water beneath it.
Sparser than trees' own density would look right here — most rivers are
only a few cells wide, so the same per-cell rate reads far denser on a
narrow water strip than it does scattered across a wide green area. Cut
to 1/4 of the first-pass value (0.015) after that read as boats covering
the water, not scattered on it.
Ambient cars on major roads. Motorway/primary/secondary only,
deliberately: ordinary neighborhood streets and pedestrian ways
(ROAD_DEFAULT, PEDESTRIAN) are dense and everywhere a user might want to
build, and a car parked in the middle of one reads as "in the way" far
more than the same car sitting on a major road's shoulder does.
"align_transport" orientation is what keeps these lined up with the road
instead of facing a random direction, which would otherwise read as a
crash, not traffic. Only the transport channel matters: transport always
wins last in the terrain paint, so a cell whose transport is one of these
renders (and therefore counts) as that road type regardless of whatever
land/water/structure value sits underneath it.
Much sparser than trees/boats: a highway with a car every couple of
cells would read as gridlock, not ambient traffic.
Occasional trains on rail lines. rail_main only (not RAIL_SUBWAY —
that's underground, wrong context for a surface-scattered prop). Same
"align_transport" reasoning as car applies: a train lying across the rail
sideways would read as derailed. Only the transport channel matters.
Very sparse, deliberately — trains are meant to read as occasional, not
as a train sitting on every visible stretch of track.
